note: The 5th and the octave by ear (intervals:1), in one ear game at "level": "new" with a Stage choice whose next stage adds the two 3rds: the text says what comfortable is before the next stage, names the Stage selector and what Start begins again, and what to do when a stage is too hard. Answers are named as the game's buttons show them, with the plain word beside each.

exercise.title: 5th or octave, by ear
exercise.why: The octave is the same note again, higher, and the 5th is the widest gap inside a chord, so these two are the easiest to tell apart and the ones to measure every other interval against.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below to hear two notes, one after the other. Pick P5 for a 5th or P8 for an octave. Press Replay in the game to hear them again before you answer.
When the name comes before you think about it, try the next stage: it adds the two 3rds, M3 for a major 3rd and m3 for a minor 3rd. Use the Stage selector below to change the stage, then press Start to hear the first pair.
If the 3rds get mixed up, go back a stage and listen only for the 5th and the octave again.
